did_you_know.text: Did you know? Ahaz was twenty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned in Jerusalem for sixteen years. The text emphasizes that he did not do what was right in the eyes of the LORD.

Did you know? Ahaz followed the ways of the kings of Israel and even passed his sons through the fire, a practice the text describes as an abomination of the nations that had been driven out before the Israelites.
Did you know? During Ahaz’s reign, Judah was defeated by both the king of Aram and the king of Israel, and many captives were taken from it.
Did you know? Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, killed 120,000 people from Judah in one day; the text connects the defeat with Judah’s abandonment of the LORD.
Did you know? The Israelites took 200,000 captives from Judah—women, sons, and daughters—as well as a great deal of plunder, and brought them to Samaria.

Did you know? The prophet Oded went out to meet the army of Israel in Samaria and warned that the killing of the people of Judah and the captives taken from them had been done in the fury of the LORD’s anger.
Did you know? After Oded’s rebuke, the soldiers left the captives and the plunder before the officials and the entire assembly instead of taking them into Samaria.
Did you know? The leaders of Ephraim cared for the captives: they clothed the naked, fed and gave them drink, anointed them with oil, and transported the weak on donkeys all the way to Jericho.
Did you know? Ahaz gave the king of Assyria treasures from the temple of the LORD, the royal palace, and the officials’ homes in order to obtain help, but it did not benefit him.
Did you know? After his death, Ahaz was buried in Jerusalem, but not in the tombs of the kings of Israel; his son Hezekiah succeeded him as king.
